newsitem.title: BELGIUM: After Finnish link, ERM spotlight moves to Italy.
newsitem.headline: After Finnish link, ERM spotlight moves to Italy.

text.p: Finland's entry into the European Union's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) means focus will now shift to currencies still outside, especially to the Italian lira but also the Swedish crown.

With Saturday's agreement to join the EU currency grid, Finland has proclaimed its determination to be in the first wave of countries to join economic and monetary union (EMU) at its planned start in 1999.

Helsinki's decision was "not a surprise and confirms the positive political sentiment in favour of European monetary union throughout Europe and will now focus attention on when the lira will enter the system," said Gerrard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International in London.
Currency stability is an EMU condition. EU heavyweights France and Germany also argue the Union's Maastricht treaty requires ERM membership in order to qualify for membership of the single currency.
By linking the markka more for political than economic reasons, Finland -- which joined the EU less than two years ago -- has shown it accepts this view.
In the currency grid, "Finland is going to have greater chances of being sure to fulfil all of the criteria," Johnny Akerholm, under-secretary of state at the Finnish finance ministry, told Reuters.
The ERM, which limits currency fluctuations to at most 15 percent up or down, now groups 11 of the EU's 15 currencies. Sweden, Britain, Italy and Greece remain outside.

Finland's action could see renewed political pressure on those not in the grid although Sweden and Britain argue currency stability, rather than ERM membership itself, should determine whether or not a country qualifies for the single currency.
